expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'are you sure?' modal as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: "The proposed 'Are you sure?' modal is not recommended."

expectations.text: Explains habituation or click-through blindness as why frequent dialogs stop working
expectations.evidence: "users quickly develop click-through blindness, clicking 'Confirm' reflexively."

expectations.text: Recommends reversibility (soft delete with a retention window) as the strongest option
expectations.evidence: "Make it reversible (Soft Delete - Rung 1 Control): The strongest device. Instead of deleting immediately, we move the workspace to a 'Trash' state with a retention period (e.g., 30 days)."

expectations.text: Recommends grace-period undo as a strong low-friction option
expectations.evidence: Grace-period undo is not mentioned; trash state is discussed but not a time-limited undo button

expectations.text: Recommends type-the-workspace-name confirmation for the irreversible case
expectations.evidence: "Type-to-Confirm (Rung 2 Warning): If deletion must be genuinely irreversible, require the user to type the workspace's exact name to confirm."

expectations.text: If a dialog is retained, requires it to name the workspace and the scale of what is lost
expectations.evidence: Option 3 explicitly requires: "Name the object: 'Delete workspace production-api'?" and "State the scale: 'This will permanently delete 14 projects and 3,201 files.'"

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the deletion rules, not just the UI
expectations.evidence: No explicit mention of server-side enforcement; verification plan only addresses UI-level bypass prevention

expectations.text: Gives an explicit preference order rather than an undifferentiated list of ideas
expectations.evidence: "Please select from the following alternatives in order of preference:" followed by numbered options; Option 1 labeled "The strongest device"
